properties.areaDesc: Mobile Coastal
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 2 at 2:51AM CDT until October 2 at 8:00AM CDT by NWS Mobile AL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding
expected with water levels up to 2 feet above normally dry
ground during tonight's high tide cycle.

* WHERE...Mobile Coastal County.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Monday evening.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 8 AM CDT this morning.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Rip currents can sweep even
the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Around 2 feet MHHW, water begins to cover
portions of Shell Belt and Coden Belt Roads. Roads may have some
debris washed up on them.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Harris, TX
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 2 at 2:51AM CDT by NWS Houston/Galveston TX
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Houston/Galveston has issued a
Flood Warning for the following rivers in Texas...

South Mayde Creek Near Greenhouse Road affecting Harris County.

For the Addicks Reservoir...including Greenhouse Road...Minor
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...South Mayde Creek near Greenhouse Road.

* WHEN...From early this morning until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 107.0 feet, At levels above 107 feet minor lowland
flooding begins as water escapes the main channel above the gage.
At 109.0 feet, At levels above 109 feet moderate lowland flooding
begins as Greenhouse Road north and south of the channel is
inundated and numerous roads along the creek are inundated and
impassable. Much of Cullen Park and Saums Road is also flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:35 AM CDT Friday the stage was 107.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 104.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage early
this morning and continue rising to 108.4 feet this morning.
Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 107.9 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 108.4
feet on 09/21/2013.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/hgx.

The next statement will be issued this afternoon at 300 PM CDT.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Devils River At Pafford Crossing nr Comstock affecting Val Verde

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Devils River at Pafford Crossing nr Comstock.

* WHEN...Until late tonight.

* IMPACTS...At 8.0 feet, (2.4 meters), Moderate flooding covers
several hundred yards of the flood plain. Campers, automobiles and
equipment can be washed downstream below Juno to Amistad Reservoir.
Livestock should be moved from flood prone areas of the flood
plain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:15 AM CDT Friday the stage was 8.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 4.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 2:15 AM CDT Friday was 8.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 8.5 feet
early this morning. It will then fall below flood stage this
afternoon.
- Flood stage is 5.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 8.1
feet on 07/11/1988.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

20 NM...
St. Andrews Bay Waterways...

Santa Rosa Beach.

properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued October 2 at 12:32AM PDT until October 8 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions with high temperatures ranging
from the mid 80s to around 90 near the coast to the mid 90s to
around 100 near higher coastal terrain expected. Nights will be
very warm with low temperatures mostly in the 70s.

* WHERE...Orange County Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...From 10 AM this morning to 8 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

properties.areaDesc: Louisa, IA; Muscatine, IA; Washington, IA
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 2 at 1:56AM CDT until October 2 at 11:30AM CDT by NWS Quad Cities IA IL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Muscatine County in east central Iowa...
Louisa County in southeastern Iowa...
Washington County in southeastern Iowa...

* WHEN...Until 1130 AM CDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Numerous roads
remain closed due to flooding. Streams continue to rise due to
excess runoff from earlier rainfall. Low-water crossings are
inundated with water and may not be passable. Expect many areas of
slow moving or standing water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 150 AM CDT, Rainfall has diminished throughout the warned
area. Total rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches or more have
occurred across the warned area resulting in flooding. As a
result, local law enforcement reported several roads either
partially inundated, or totally inundated with standing water and
some are closed.
- Flooding impacts will continue, but no additional rainfall is
expected.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Nebraska...

Republican River At Guide Rock affecting Nuckolls and Webster
Counties.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is currently ongoing and will be expected to
continue until this evening.

* WHERE...Little Blue River near Deweese, including the reach of the
river from near Deweese to near Oak.

* IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, Highway 78 south of the bridge will be
impacted along with numerous county roads including River Road as
well as Road B and E. In addition, a home will be threatened
downstream on the south side of the river off of Road 3600 south of
Superior. This home required sandbagging during the July flooding
of 2019 when the river crest at Guide Rock reached 15.1 feet.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:30 AM CDT Friday the stage was 13.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 10.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 1:30 AM CDT Friday was 13.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 14.0 feet
Friday morning. It will then fall below flood stage late Friday
afternoon.
- Flood stage is 12.5 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 14.1
feet on 05/25/2008.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.areaDesc: City and Borough of Juneau
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 1 at 9:30PM AKDT until October 3 at 7:45AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
The second release from Suicide Basin is ongoing. Based on an
observed earlier start time of water draining from the basin, the
crest time for the Mendenhall Lake and River has been adjusted to
early Friday morning. Minor to moderate flooding continues to be
expected near Mendenhall Lake and River Thursday night into Friday
morning.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by a glacier-dammed lake outburst continues.

* WHERE...The Mendenhall Lake And River near the Mendenhall Glacier
Recreation area, View Drive and below Back Loop bridge.

* WHEN...Until 745 AM AKDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the area around Mendenhall Lake and along the
Mendenhall River is imminent or occurring. Water levels will,
continue to rise and water temperatures will fall within the lake,
and river.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 920 PM AKDT, gauge data reported a glacier-dammed lake
outburst. Flooding is expected to begin shortly, especially near
The Mendenhall Lake And River.
- The outburst flood forecast is based on an estimated volume of
water in the glacier dammed lake and an estimated release rate
based on previous events. The extent of water drainage within the
basin (partial or full) can vary widely between outburst flood
events and is a major source of uncertainty in the forecast,
particularly with regard to the peak flood stage.
- For Mendenhall Lake :
At 8:30pm the stage was 7.7 feet.
Flood Stage is 9.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest around 9.8 to 10.3 feet is expected between 5
to 9am Friday. Water levels will go above minor flood stage of 9
feet around 2am Friday. Water levels will reach moderate flood
stage of 10 feet around 5 to 9am Friday. Water levels will fall
below minor flood stage late morning Friday.

Impacts:
At 7.7 feet: Nugget Falls trail begins to flood near the beginning of
the trail. Along the Mendenhall River some sections will experience
bank erosion resulting in dangerous tree fall. These conditions could
make floating the river more hazardous with the higher water levels.
At 9.0 feet: Water starts to cover Skaters Cabin Road between Skaters
Cabin and West Glacier Trailhead, also water will flow into the
Mendenhall Lake Campground.
At 9.5 feet: Water levels up to 0.5 feet will cover Skaters Cabin
Road between Skaters Cabin and West Glacier Trailhead. Campsite 7
will be flooded with water starting to flow over the road between
campsites 8 and 9 in the Mendenhall Campground.
At 10.0 feet: Water levels will inundate Mendenhall Campground with
up to 3 feet of water covering low areas as well as up to 1.5 feet of
water covering Skaters Cabin Road. Portions of West Glacier Trail
will be impassable. Areas along View Dr will start to flood and cause
minor flooding of yards. Closure of pedestrian pathways beneath
Brotherhood Bridge and the trail system on the west side of
Mendenhall River during outburst events.
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

The cold water temperatures can increase the threat of hypothermia
and lower the time required to cause hypothermia.

properties.headline: Tropical Storm Warning issued October 2 at 2:54PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
...TROPICAL STORM CHOI-WAN SLOWLY MOVING WEST-NORTHWEST AND INCHING
CLOSER TO ALAMAGAN...

.NEW INFORMATION...
None.

.AREAS AFFECTED...
This local statement provides information and recommended actions
for people on Saipan, Tinian, Agrihan, Pagan and Alamagan in the
Commonwealth of the Northern Marianas.

.WATCHES/WARNINGS...
A Tropical Storm Warning remains in effect for Saipan, Tinian and
their adjacent coastal waters, as well as Alamagan, Pagan, and
Agrihan in the CNMI. A Typhoon Watch remains in effect for Alamagan,
Pagan, and Agrihan in the CNMI.

A Typhoon Watch means that typhoon conditions, including winds of 74
mph or more, are possible within 48 hours.
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected within 24 hours.

A Flood Watch remains in effect for Tinian and Saipan. Please listen
closely for any Flash Flood Warnings that might be in effect for
your area.

Please check the latest public and marine forecasts for detailed
information about additional hazards.

.STORM INFORMATION...
At 1 PM ChST, the center of Tropical Storm Choi-wan (26W) was
located near latitude 17.2N and longitude 144.7E. This was about 260
miles north of Guam. Choi-wan is moving west-northwest at 5 mph, slowing
down before pivoting toward the north-northeast with little change
in forward speed through Saturday as it moves up the Far Northern
Marianas. Maximum sustained winds have increased to 65 mph. Choi-wan
is forecast to intensify through tonight, possibly becoming a
typhoon later today. Tropical storm force winds continue to extend
outward from the center up to 125 miles, however, the wind field is
expected to expand farther south over the next few hours.

.SITUATION OVERVIEW...
Tropical Storm Choi-wan continues to move away from Anatahan and is
inching closer to Alamagan, pivoting slowly to the north-northeast
through Saturday. During this time, the wind field will continue to
expand, exposing Tinian and Saipan in Tropical Storm condition a
little longer, now through Saturday. While showers have tapered a
little earlier in the day, rainbands that pummeled Guam and Rota
earlier this morning are now being pulled toward Tinian and Saipan,
with more intense showers and thunderstorms expected tonight.
properties.instruction:
Stay indoors during heavy rain and tropical storm-force wind
conditions associated with Tropical Storm Choi-wan (26W). Heed the
advice of your local emergency managers and officials, and
continue to monitor forecasts by the National Weather Service
office in Tiyan, Guam. Remain in sturdy shelter until the all-
clear is given.

Preparations for Tropical Storm Choi-wan should be complete, or
rapidly rushed to completion. Take small loose object indoors.
Remain in suitable shelter, such as a cave or sturdy concrete
structure. Shelter in place until the all- clear is given.

.WIND INFORMATION...
North to northeast winds of 25 to 35 mph will turn toward the
southeast and increase today as Choi-wan pivots north across the
northern CNMI and strengthens, potentially becoming a typhoon later
today to the west of Alamagan and Pagan. Tropical storm force winds
of 39 to 50 mph look to continue through Sunday. Depending on the
track and intensity, winds may increase to strong tropical storm-
force of 58 to 65 mph early Saturday morning. Typhoon force winds
greater than 74 mph look to remain possible during closest passage.

.COASTAL INUNDATION AND SURF INFORMATION...
Hazardous surf of 8 to 12 feet along east-facing and south facing
reefs are expected to continue, to then spread along north and west-
facing reefs as the center moves north-northeast parallel to the
northern CNMI tonight through Saturday night, increasing by several
feet during this time. As Choi-wan continues to strengthen, surf will
continue to increase, likely becoming dangerous by early next week.
Significant coastal erosion and some coastal inundation is expected
during Choi- wan's passage.

.OTHER STORM EFFECTS...
Periods of rain, widespread heavy showers and scattered
thunderstorms are expected through tonight, which is expected to
produce rainfall totals of 8 to 14 inches by early Monday morning,
with up to 20 inches of rainfall possible near the center of the
system.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of
10 to 14 feet expected in the surf zone. For the Coastal Flood
Watch, significant coastal flooding possible. For the High Rip
Current Risk, dangerous rip currents expected.

* WHERE...North and West facing reefs of Tinian and Saipan.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 4 AM ChST Monday. For the
Coastal Flood Watch, through Monday evening. For the High Rip
Current Risk, through late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure may
be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur. Dangerous
swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Rip currents will be life threatening. Inexperienced swimmers
should remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions.
If caught in a rip current, relax and float. Don't swim against
the current. If able, swim in a direction following the
shoreline. If unable to escape, face the shore and call or wave
for help.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 1 at 11:34PM CDT until October 2 at 7:30PM CDT by NWS Hastings NE
properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor Flooding along portions of the Little Blue River in
Thayer and Nuckolls counties

* WHERE...East Central Nuckolls County in south central Nebraska...
Northern Thayer County in south central Nebraska...

* WHEN...Until 730 PM CDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations continues.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1104 PM CDT, automated river gauges continue to indicate that
minor flooding is occurring along the Little Blue River as a
result of heavy rainfall over the last few days. At 10:15 PM CDT,
a gauge along the Little Blue River at Hebron reported a stage of
14.0 feet, which was 0.5 feet above the minor flood stage of 13.5
feet. As a result, minor flooding continues both upstream and
downstream of Hebron along the Little Blue River through Thayer
County. Since the river crested at 14.9 feet around 8AM Thursday
morning, water levels have continued to gradually fall. Though
water levels appear to be falling at the gauge site at Hebron,
water levels upstream at the gauge site near Deshler, however,
still continue to just barely rise. As of 10:45PM CDT, the
upstream gauge near Deshler rests at 16.4 feet, just barely into
the minor flood stage starting at 16 feet. It is uncertain how
much water is still left to collect upstream, though recent water
level increases have appeared to of substantially slowed. This
leads us to believe that water levels may be soon to crest
tonight. Minor flooding along the stretch of the Little Blue
river across Thayer and Nuckolls county will be expected to
continue on through the night and into a portion of the day
Friday.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Dry Creek, South Fork Big Sandy Creek, Little Blue River, Little
Sandy Creek, Oak Creek, Walnut Creek, Elk Creek, Turtle Creek,
Spring Creek, Dry Sandy Creek and Big Sandy Creek.
- Some locations that could experience flooding include...
Hebron, Davenport, Bruning, Alexandria, Carleton, Oak and
Belvidere.

Elder, KS.

* WHERE...Southwestern Jewell County in north central Kansas...
North Central Mitchell County in north central Kansas...

* WHEN...Until noon CDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is ongoing.

minor flooding continues along the Solomon River in the Glen
Elder area, as a result of heavy rainfall over the last few days.

stage of 22.5 feet, which was 1.5 feet above the minor flood

tonight, though it will likely take until Friday afternoon before
the water levels fall back below the minor flood stage.

Little Walnut Creek, Elm Creek, Solomon River, Ash Creek, Frog
Creek, Browns Creek, Limestone Creek, West Limestone Creek,
Granite Creek, Disappointment Creek and Turkey Creek.
- Some locations that could experience flooding include...
Glen Elder and Ionia, but this Warning is mainly geared toward
minor flooding along the Solomon River in the Glen Elder area.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

rainfall forecast, or any additional rainfall after 48 hours, may
cause changes to these river forecasts.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 1 at 6:55PM CDT until October 2 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Houston/Galveston TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of south central and southeast Texas, including
the following areas, in south central Texas, Coastal Jackson and
Inland Jackson. In southeast Texas, Coastal Harris, Fort Bend,
Grimes, Inland Harris, Montgomery, Walker, Waller and Wharton.

* WHEN...Through Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Showers and thunderstorms capable of producing heavy downpours
will impact the watch area through Friday evening. Embedded
training rain rates of 2-4 inches per hour will be possible with
the deep tropical airmass overhead. Locations that experience
training storms with heavier rainfall rates may  experience rapid
runoff that could result in flash flooding. Those living in areas
prone to flooding should be prepared to take action should
flooding develop. Stay weather aware and be ready to take action
when Flash Flood Warnings are issued, particularly wireless
emergency alert Flash Flood Warnings for considerable and/or
catastrophic flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 1 at 1:10PM EDT until October 2 at 4:00AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and rough surf.

* WHERE...The beaches of Volusia, Brevard, Indian River, Saint
Lucie, and Martin Counties.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.
